A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniOD work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across renumbering and reorganization. Internal reporting inconsistencies in v2 are observable document issues, rather than extraction gaps.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original UniOD detection results, runtime measurements and ablations. Some baseline results are borrowed, but UniOD's own empirical results clearly qualify.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix H report original detection experiments, reversed training/testing groups, domain-exclusion analyses, large-dataset evaluations and results on 27 additional datasets.

M1.justification: The Gaussian similarity matrices, SVD features, parallel GIN/GT architecture, classifier, cross-entropy objective and training augmentation remain unchanged. Appendix H.10 adds a limited inference adaptation: randomly partitioning large datasets into disjoint subsets and applying UniOD independently to each partition.

E1.justification: Appendix H.11 adds evaluation on 27 ADBench datasets beyond the original 30-dataset training/testing pool, including CIFAR10, MVTec-AD, agnews and 20news (Tables 18–19). This substantially expands represented data coverage. Reversing the original two groups is separately a protocol change.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated comparators MetaOD, MLP+TF and LODA, extending comparisons to model selection and another learned approach using historical datasets. ODIM is removed from the reported comparisons. IF, LOF and OC-SVM remain evaluated in Appendix Tables 9–10 despite their omission from the shortened main tables.

E3.justification: The main baseline comparison changes from recommended or published best-performing configurations to grid search on historical datasets, with default configurations retained separately. V2 adds reversed training/testing groups, a 6,000-sample cap for the reversed-group evaluation, domain-exclusion training conditions and partitioned large-dataset testing. UniOD's stated architecture and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds baseline hyperparameter-sensitivity heatmaps, default-versus-tuned comparisons, historical-domain exclusion, representation visualizations and large-dataset analyses. The bandwidth, historical-dataset-count and subsampling ablation tables retain identical numerical entries after relocation. The separate SVD+MLP architecture ablation in v1 Appendix E.4 is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report means over five runs for the principal comparison. Neither provides seed identities, standard deviations, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2's explicit five-run table captions do not establish additional repetitions or a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds tuned-baseline results, reversed-group results and extensive additional evaluations. Newly reported UniOD averages are 78.52/36.69 AUROC/AUPRC on Group II and 74.9/35.7 on the additional 27 datasets. The original main-comparison averages remain 78.93/45.43. Much of v1's default comparison reappears in Table 11, but with altered entries and misaligned labels; these are not evidence of same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V1 provides complexity analysis but no generalization theorem. V2 introduces Theorem 4.1, a norm-dependent generalization bound under bounded Lipschitz-loss assumptions, with covering-number, Rademacher-complexity and attention-related arguments in Appendices A–B. The runtime complexity expressions are also revised.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list add theoretical guarantees of effectiveness as a central contribution, absent from v1. The stated main evaluation expands from 15 datasets against 15 baselines to 30 datasets against 17 baselines. The underlying claim of a universal detector requiring no target-dataset retraining remains.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations of domain-exclusion robustness, difficulties transferring tuned hyperparameters, t-SNE distortions and the generalization bound's implications. It removes v1's dedicated limitations paragraph while acknowledging GPU-memory constraints in H.10. Its performance discussion shifts from acknowledging IF's AUPRC advantage to claiming best averages, although the full comparison in Table 9 still favors IF on AUPRC.

D1.justification: V2 supplies explicit per-method hyperparameter grids and MetaOD configuration information in Appendix G/Table 8, describes MLP+TF construction, and adds a UniOD code-repository link. These materially expand reproducibility information. Existing UniOD network dimensions, optimizer settings, training epochs and hardware disclosures are relocated to H.2 without substantive changes.

R1.justification: The literature coverage is substantially revised: v2 adds heterogeneous-attribute meta-learning and tabular-foundation references, learning-theory sources supporting the new proofs, and recent missing-data, graph and fairness work. Numerous distinct normalizing-flow and ICA references are removed. The central positioning against dataset-specific detection and conventional transfer learning remains.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract and portions of the introduction, methodology and experimental narrative, compresses numbered related-work subsections into shorter paragraphs, and establishes a separate theoretical-analysis section. Algorithm 1 and implementation details move to the appendices, whose organization is substantially expanded and revised.

P2.justification: V2 redraws and relocates Figure 1, adds eight hyperparameter-sensitivity panels and three t-SNE plots, and combines the earlier ablation figures into Figure 4. Benchmark tables are reorganized with colored ranking highlights, and numerous comparison and robustness tables are added. The framework diagram is retained with renumbering. Table 11 introduces malformed and misaligned rows.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central generalization claim through reversed training/testing groups, source-domain exclusion and 27 additional datasets, addressing v1's reliance on one test group. Historical-data tuning, relevant new comparators and explicit search spaces also improve comparison quality and reproducibility. These gains outweigh reporting defects, but conclusions require qualification: Table 9 gives IF higher AUPRC than UniOD (47.59 versus 45.43), and Table 11 contains malformed and misaligned rows.
